reason: This optional closed-book diagnostic tests shape, loss, gradient, masking and leakage reasoning; supplying those diagrams before the attempt would answer the questions. Its answer panel gives exact values, and the corresponding teaching lessons receive concept figures.
The one-position offset is a spatial indexing contract: align input tokens, next-token targets and logit rows without solving the diagnostic example.
An indexed mask makes the permitted triangle, diagonal and softmax axis directly inspectable against the future-perturbation test.
The two skip connections make normalization order and the distinct x/u residual operands visible.
A complete decoder and optional shared embedding/head tensor resolve where the final normalization belongs and why tied weights count once.

Independent review identified a missing mechanism beyond the scalar update checklist: decoupled weight decay and gradient-derived moments follow separate parameter-update paths. The dependency diagram makes that distinction without solving the numeric exercise.
The generate/append loop and EOS, length and context-limit exits are branching behavior that a simple operation list obscures.
Parallel uninterrupted and save/reload timelines show exactly which state and remaining updates must match.
RMSNorm reduces only one token row; SwiGLU splits into two differently transformed branches before an elementwise product. Both need their own shape diagram.
A geometric pair rotation reveals norm preservation and rotation direction without replacing the relative-position derivation.
Head-to-KV incidence is the essential nontrivial mapping and explains the repeat-interleave pitfall.
A composition map shows the separate Q/K rotary and unrotated V paths, residuals and modern MLP at the integration boundary.
The key-splitting branches show one draw per consumed subkey and avoid implying a mutable random generator.
A batched input grid and shared parameter vector make the mapped versus unmapped argument axes explicit.
A nonsquare value-labeled matrix makes the transpose mapping inspectable, including a bug that square shapes could conceal.

The shared nonuniform probe is explicitly defined as sum(output * fixed_probe); the required input/parameter gradient error table and optional finite-difference calculation expose actual discrepancies more precisely than a generic backpropagation diagram.
A parameter-tree and explicit argument diagram separates array ownership from the pure decoder computation.
Aligned framework lanes make the first divergent activation boundary visible rather than presenting only final logit error.
A state feedback loop exposes the requirement to feed returned optimizer moments/counter/RNG into the next call.
A quantitative threshold plot explains why the absolute term controls comparisons near zero; it does not replace measured parity errors.
A position-indexed cache trace distinguishes retained prefix entries from newly appended entries and their absolute rotary positions.
Two aligned prefix paths show which logit rows correspond after an appended token, including a nonzero position offset.
A document-to-chunk partition picture makes overlapping-chunk leakage and split-before-chunking concrete.
A host/device timeline separates warm-up, dispatch and completion, explaining the denominator of the measured pilot rate.
Factor dimensions and the frozen/shared input branch explain the low-rank update and which tensors train.

Merging requires branch disabling to avoid double application, while initialization has a distinct asymmetric gradient mechanism. Show merge state up front and the derived gradient paths inside the answer disclosure.

The task is loading a chosen pinned checkpoint and recording its exact tokenizer/configuration. A manifest of real revision, token IDs, device and special-token settings is clearer and safer than a generic model-loading chain.
A snapshot/fork/restore diagram distinguishes the disposable smoke update, merged evaluation copy and pristine start of SFT.
A template-by-entity family grid reveals cross-split family leakage that complete-string deduplication cannot detect.
A token/logit/label alignment grid makes the first supervised target and internal shifting semantics explicit.
The training/validation/held-out data boundaries show which split updates weights, selects checkpoints or measures final outcomes.

The deliverable is a paired table of actual baseline/adapted outcomes and separate validity/correctness counts. Invented example bars or transitions could be mistaken for results; the learner’s measured table and error examples should carry this lesson.
Separate stored-weight and per-token-use markings prevent the key misconception that top-2 halves stored expert memory.
A router-to-expert graph makes the selected-only softmax and weighted parallel expert paths explicit.
A labeled expert-output tensor slice and sparse weight row show the broadcast and reduction axis of the independent reference.

The student must compute actual ordinary/skewed expert count tables and verify their sum. A supplied balanced/skewed histogram would substitute hypothetical outcomes for the experiment; the routing mechanism is already visualized in the implementation lesson.
MLA has genuine content/position and query/KV branching with head-shared versus per-head dimensions; a projection diagram prevents omitted or repeated axes.
A two-term score diagram separates retained latent/positional state, transformed query values and shared learned weights.
A common-scale cache chart makes retained-state size and context doubling visible; the exact worked exercise answer belongs inside the answer disclosure.

This synthesis assembles the learner’s projection trace, persistent-cache walkthrough and byte calculation, each supported by the preceding concept figures. Another generic compression drawing would repeat those mechanisms instead of auditing the actual note and evidence-depth labels.
A schematic inventory contrasts per-layer recurrent matrix state with attention token history, without inventing a Qwen layer pattern.
The matrix trace shows decay versus the key-directed column correction; move the complete worked arithmetic into the answer disclosure.
A fixed-plus-growing storage plot makes hybrid total memory distinguishable from recurrent-state memory; exact toy values belong in the answer disclosure.

The work is to connect the existing component inventory, recurrence arithmetic and storage table, then qualify retrieval and performance claims. The three preceding visuals supply the mechanisms; prose is needed for limits that a memory cartoon cannot establish.

The learner selects a named Gemma variant and fills a source-linked mechanism table. A fixed architecture diagram could silently choose a different variant or imply unsupported details; the student’s variant-specific comparison table is the correct visual representation.
Contrasting cache-width compression with selecting prior positions clarifies two independent design axes without substituting for the report-specific table.

A two-path multimodal merge clarifies the representation interface. Inside the answer disclosure, a compact exact-comparison table also distinguishes SFT targets, DPO preference pairs and GRPO rewarded groups plus their different reference/baseline roles.

This Day0 reference is an editing/evidence-depth guide for the student’s two-page comparison. Its existing component table and previously constructed interface drawing carry the information; a new course diagram would duplicate the student’s deliverable.

The fair-study contract is an exact configuration and parameter-count comparison table. Query/KV sharing is already taught visually; a new head drawing with different counts would not clarify controls, timing settings or the absence of quality matching better than that table.
Separate equality edges identify valid own-model cache references and GQA expanded-KV parity without implying independently parameterized MHA/GQA logits should match.
A cache-length timeline separates prompt prefill from incremental decode and shows why each repetition restarts at the same context length.

This report must display the student’s measured cache and prefill/decode tables or plots, with spread and sample count. No universal latency curve is warranted; fabricated illustrative performance data would distract from the actual raw samples.
Two branches from the same initial state expose the controlled weight-decay intervention and common token stream.

The main activity is running the bounded baseline and inspecting its actual token-counted curves and checkpoint metadata. A supplied learning curve would not validate those artifacts; the earlier checkpoint comparison and ablation fork already explain the state contract.

The ablation must use the already frozen two-arm design. The existing fork figure explains common initialization; today’s configuration diff, first-batch identifiers and exact token endpoints provide stronger evidence than repeating the same diagram.

The explicitly required student-generated training/validation plots at matched consumed tokens are the appropriate visuals. Adding invented loss curves would bias interpretation of the genuine small-seed experiment.

This reference task inventories concrete revision hashes, tokenizer identities, layouts, data and expected outputs. A manifest and conversion table expose missing inputs directly; a generic dependency graph would hide those exact identities.
The task is executing documented commands in a clean environment and preserving the first real failure. Commands and the setup transcript are more actionable than an installation flowchart.

The learner already has training/parity entry points and must create fresh outputs. The new learning curve and numerical error report are the relevant visuals; a simple train-then-parity chain would add little and failure branching is addressed in 15-4.
A branching gate diagram makes any required child failure terminate the wrapper instead of reaching a success summary.

Model/data cards must report actual parameter counts, provenance and limitations in separate sections for scratch and pretrained artifacts. Structured text and linked manifests communicate those exact facts better than a generic provenance picture.

The report explicitly requires small figures or tables from actual measured results, with configuration/raw-data/command links. Supplied synthetic result figures would not support the student’s claims.

This reference lesson is itself a student diagram-construction and verification exercise. Supplying finished diagrams for an unseen implementation risks norm/layout mismatch; earlier teaching figures are examples, while the student must draw and validate their own code-specific diagrams.
The student records an explanation using their actual report figures. A new course figure would displace rather than improve the requested walkthrough and claim audit.

Environment setup and the fixed matrix/autograd smoke script are best expressed as commands and exact expected outputs. Matrix axes and broadcasting receive a dedicated figure in the optional tensor refresher.
A small nonsquare value grid shows which axis the length-three bias broadcasts across, while leaving the learner to write independent tests.

This is closed-book retrieval of attention shapes, RoPE and functional state. Displaying those diagrams would cue the answers; corrected reasoning should be compared with the earlier mechanism figures and the student’s tests.

The appropriate debugging fixture depends on the learner’s specific blocked prerequisite. A fixed flowchart would restate the short select/minimize/repair/save checklist without identifying the actual tensor or failed condition.

This closed-book cache/LoRA/masking assessment should require the learner to reconstruct relationships unaided. The teaching lessons contain the relevant figures; the answer panel and saved tests are the better post-attempt check.

This optional repair reference is driven by the learner’s current failure, not a fixed architecture. The explicit smallest-test and next-command instructions are clearer than a generic decision diagram.

This retrieval checkpoint assesses stored/active experts, MLA cache and hybrid state. Supplying those diagrams would undermine reconstruction; earlier lesson figures are available for correction after the attempt.

A useful visual here would have to depict the student’s actual minimal reproducer or uncertain derivation. The current short debugging checklist appropriately leaves that choice to the observed blocker.

This spare-capacity reference can end early when there is no blocker. A prescribed diagram would add an artificial activity; the saved minimal failure, corrected explanation and next command are the intended evidence.

The final defense asks for closed-book equations and implementation connections. A supplied decoder or cache diagram would cue the assessment; use the learner’s own code-linked evidence after the answers.

The reviewer smoke run is checked through an actual fresh-clone transcript and newly generated curve/parity artifacts. The failure-gate visual in 15-4 already explains propagation; repeating it would not detect hidden inputs.

The observed upstream friction is intentionally unspecified. A useful figure must come from the real minimal reproducer; repository instructions, versioned behavior and a focused patch are more precise than a generic contribution pipeline.
The release is a linked index of the learner’s actual diagrams, reports and evidence. A new stock portfolio diagram would not improve the required traceability or completion decision.
